Methods and embodiments are provided for a tandem mass spectrometer designed for extremely large charge throughput, up to 1E+10 ions/sec. In one mode of operation, the initial ion flow, spanning a wide m/z range, is temporally separated in a trap array. The array ejects ions within a narrower instantaneous m/z range. The ion flow is then collected and confined in a wide-bore ion channel with limited temporal spread. The ion flow with the narrow m/z range is subsequently analyzed in a multi-reflecting TOF at frequent, time-encoded operation of the orthogonal accelerator, thereby forming multiple non-overlapping spectral segments.  

In another mode, temporally separated ions are subjected to fragmentation for comprehensive, all-mass MS-MS analysis. The instantaneous ion flow at the MR-TOF entrance is characterized by a lower spectral population, which enables efficient decoding of overlapping spectra. These modes are combined with conventional spectrometer operation to improve dynamic range. To provide a practical solution, multiple novel components are proposed, including trap arrays, wide-bore confining channels, resistive multipoles, and a long-life TOF detector.
outputs.L2:
Methods and embodiments are disclosed for a tandem mass spectrometer configured to handle extremely high charge throughput, up to 1E+10 ions per second. In one operating mode, an incoming ion stream spanning a broad m/z range is separated over time within an array of traps. This trap array releases ions in temporarily narrower m/z windows. The resulting ion flow is gathered and confined in a wide-bore ion channel while maintaining restricted temporal dispersion. The ion stream, now covering a narrower m/z range, is subsequently examined in a multi-reflecting time-of-flight mass analyzer using frequent, time-encoded operation of an orthogonal accelerator, thereby generating multiple spectral segments that do not overlap.

In another operating mode, the time-separated ions undergo fragmentation to enable comprehensive all-mass MS-MS analysis. At the entrance to the MR-TOF analyzer, the instantaneous ion flow has a reduced spectral population, which permits effective decoding of overlapping spectra. These modes may be used together with conventional spectrometer operation to enhance dynamic range. To make the system practical, several new components are proposed, including trap arrays, wide-bore confining channels, a resistive multipole, and a long-life TOF detector.
outputs.L3:
The method describes a tandem mass spectrometer configured for extremely high ion throughput, with a capacity of up to approximately 1E+10 ions per second. This high-throughput capability is intended to allow efficient analysis of very large ion populations while preserving mass-spectrometric performance and enabling both MS and MS-MS measurements.

In one mode of operation, the instrument receives a broad ion flow covering a wide mass-to-charge ratio, or m/z, range. This ion flow is introduced into a trap array, which temporarily stores and time-separates ions according to their m/z values. Instead of transmitting the entire broad m/z population at once, the trap array ejects ions in narrower, momentary m/z windows. As a result, the originally complex ion beam is converted into a sequence of time-separated ion packets, each representing a reduced m/z range.

The narrowed ion flow is then directed into a wide-bore ion channel, where it is radially confined while maintaining high transmission capacity. From there, the ions are analyzed by a multi-reflecting time-of-flight mass analyzer. The analyzer employs frequent, time-encoded orthogonal acceleration, allowing multiple ion packets to be injected and analyzed in a controlled temporal sequence. This approach supports high duty cycle operation while helping to manage the large incoming ion population.

In another operating mode, the time-separated ions are subjected to fragmentation. Because the precursor ions have already been separated in time according to m/z range, their fragment ions can be associated more effectively with the corresponding precursor windows. This enables comprehensive all-mass MS-MS analysis, in which a broad range of precursor ions is fragmented without requiring isolation of only a single selected precursor at a time. The reduced spectral population in each time segment also helps simplify the decoding of overlapping fragment spectra.

The system may combine these high-throughput modes with conventional spectrometer operation, allowing flexible use depending on the analytical task. To support these capabilities, the instrument incorporates several specialized components, including trap arrays for ion storage and timed ejection, wide-bore ion-confining channels for handling intense ion flows, resistive multipoles for controlled ion transport and confinement, and long-life time-of-flight detectors designed to tolerate high ion loads. Together, these elements provide a platform for high-throughput tandem mass spectrometry with both broad MS coverage and comprehensive MS-MS capability.
outputs.L4:
A tandem mass spectrometer is proposed that is capable of processing extremely large ion throughput while preserving mass resolving power, dynamic range, and tandem MS capability. The instrument is based on the use of multiple ion traps or trap arrays that collect ions in parallel and then release them in a controlled, time-separated manner. Instead of forcing the entire ion population through a single narrow path at one time, ions are distributed among several storage regions and wide-bore ion channels. This reduces space-charge effects, increases ion capacity, and allows a much larger total number of ions to be analyzed during a single acquisition cycle.

In operation, ions generated from a sample are accumulated in an array of traps. The contents of these traps are then ejected sequentially or in coded time patterns so that different ion packets enter the analyzer at different moments. This temporal separation lowers the instantaneous complexity of each spectrum because only a fraction of the total ion population is analyzed at any given time. As a result, peak overlap is reduced, detector saturation is minimized, and weak signals are less likely to be obscured by more abundant ions.

The mass analysis may be performed using a multi-reflection time-of-flight analyzer, or MR-TOF analyzer. In such an analyzer, ion packets undergo multiple reflections between electrostatic mirrors, greatly extending their flight path while keeping the physical size of the instrument manageable. The increased flight path improves mass resolution and mass accuracy. Because the ion packets are introduced at known times from known traps or channels, the resulting spectra can be decoded computationally, even when signals from multiple ejection events partially overlap. This makes it possible to reconstruct a complete mass spectrum from a sequence of lower-complexity measurements.

The system may also include fragmentation capability for tandem mass spectrometry. Selected ions, broad mass ranges, or even all ions across the mass range may be fragmented before analysis. This enables all-mass MS-MS operation, in which precursor and fragment information can be acquired efficiently without requiring slow, narrow precursor selection. By combining trap-array storage, time-separated release, and MR-TOF analysis, the instrument can obtain tandem mass spectra for complex samples at high speed and high sensitivity.

A key advantage of the proposed architecture is improved dynamic range. Since ions are divided among multiple traps and released in separate packets, highly abundant ions are less likely to dominate the detector response at the same instant that low-abundance ions arrive. The lower momentary spectral complexity also improves the ability of software algorithms to deconvolute overlapping signals and assign peaks correctly. This approach is especially useful for complex mixtures, high-throughput proteomics, metabolomics, environmental analysis, and other applications where many ion species must be measured over a wide concentration range.

The design is further supported by novel enabling components. Resistive multipoles may be used to guide, confine, cool, or transfer ions over extended distances while maintaining smooth electric-field gradients and high ion transmission. Wide-bore ion channels increase charge capacity and reduce losses caused by Coulomb repulsion. Long-life time-of-flight detectors are also incorporated to withstand the high ion flux associated with large-throughput operation, improving instrument robustness and reducing maintenance requirements.

Overall, the proposed tandem mass spectrometer combines parallel ion accumulation, controlled temporal encoding, high-resolution MR-TOF mass analysis, and optional fragmentation to achieve efficient analysis of very large ion populations. By reducing instantaneous spectral congestion while maintaining high total ion throughput, the instrument enables faster, more sensitive, and more accurate mass spectrometric measurements than conventional single-channel approaches.
outputs.L5:
**The Ion Method**

The ion method is a scientific approach used to study and understand charged particles known as ions. An ion forms when an atom or molecule gains or loses electrons, giving it a positive or negative charge. This process is important in many areas of science, including chemistry, physics, biology, and environmental studies.

The method often involves identifying ions in a solution or material. Scientists may use tools such as ion chromatography, mass spectrometry, or electrochemical sensors to detect and measure different ions. These techniques help researchers understand the composition of substances, monitor water quality, develop medicines, and improve industrial processes.

One important advantage of the ion method is its accuracy. By focusing on ions, scientists can gather detailed information about chemical reactions and the behavior of materials. For example, measuring sodium, calcium, or chloride ions can reveal important details about drinking water, soil health, or biological fluids.

In conclusion, the ion method plays a valuable role in modern science. The study of ions helps explain many natural and technological processes, making this method essential for research, analysis, and innovation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a tandem mass spectrometer capable of extremely high ion throughput, using trap arrays, wide-bore ion channels, MR-TOF analysis, fragmentation modes, and improved dynamic range.
counterfactuals.output: A tandem mass spectrometer is disclosed for high-throughput analysis of ions over an extended dynamic range. The system includes an ion source, one or more wide-bore ion guides or ion channels configured to transmit high ion currents with reduced space-charge losses, and a plurality of ion traps arranged in an array for parallel accumulation, storage, isolation, cooling, fragmentation, and/or timed release of ion packets. Ions from the trap array may be selectively combined or sequentially injected into a multi-reflection time-of-flight (MR-TOF) mass analyzer to provide high-resolution mass analysis at elevated duty cycle. The instrument may operate in multiple tandem mass spectrometry modes, including precursor selection, collision-induced dissociation, higher-energy collisional dissociation, electron-based fragmentation, ultraviolet photodissociation, or combinations thereof, with fragmentation performed in selected traps, transfer regions, collision cells, or dedicated reaction devices. Control electronics coordinate ion accumulation times, trap filling levels, packet compression, ejection timing, and MR-TOF injection to maintain mass accuracy and resolving power while avoiding detector saturation. Improved dynamic range is provided by parallel ion storage, ion packet splitting or attenuation, gain-selectable detection, multiplexed acquisition, and abundance-dependent routing of ions among traps or analysis cycles. The disclosed architecture enables extremely high ion throughput, efficient utilization of ion flux, rapid tandem mass spectrometric sequencing, and quantitative analysis of high-complexity samples.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention for a high-throughput tandem mass spectrometer that handles up to 1E+10 ions/sec and includes time-separated ion trapping, orthogonal acceleration, multi-reflecting TOF, and all-mass MS-MS operation.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is a high-throughput tandem mass spectrometer designed to process extremely intense ion fluxes—up to about **1×10¹⁰ ions per second**—while preserving high mass resolution, sensitivity, and MS-MS capability.

It combines several key technologies:

- **Time-separated ion trapping:** Incoming ions are accumulated in traps or trap arrays in time-separated packets, allowing very large ion currents to be handled without overwhelming downstream analyzers.
- **Orthogonal acceleration:** The trapped ion packets are pulsed sideways into a time-of-flight analyzer, improving duty cycle and enabling precise timing control.
- **Multi-reflecting time-of-flight mass analyzer:** Ions undergo multiple reflections between electrostatic mirrors, extending their flight path in a compact instrument and providing high resolving power and mass accuracy.
- **All-mass MS-MS operation:** Instead of isolating and fragmenting only one precursor mass at a time, the system can fragment and analyze ions across a broad mass range, enabling parallel tandem MS acquisition.

The system is intended to overcome space-charge limitations and duty-cycle losses common in conventional tandem mass spectrometers. By separating ion accumulation, fragmentation, and high-resolution TOF analysis in time, it can support rapid, sensitive, and comprehensive analysis of complex samples, such as proteomic or metabolomic mixtures, at very high ion throughput.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical abstract describing methods and embodiments for improving dynamic range in mass spectrometry using trap arrays, resistive multipoles, wide bore confinement channels, and long-life TOF detectors.
counterfactuals.output:
Methods and embodiments are described for improving dynamic range in mass spectrometry through distributed ion handling, controlled ion attenuation, high-capacity confinement, and extended-life ion detection. In one embodiment, ions from an ion source are accumulated, stored, or spatially distributed among a plurality of ion traps arranged as a trap array. The trap array may be operated in parallel or sequential modes to divide high ion populations into multiple packets, reduce space-charge distortion, selectively isolate ion subsets, and deliver regulated ion flux to downstream mass analyzers.

In another embodiment, one or more resistive multipole ion guides are used to provide controlled axial electric fields, dissipative ion transport, and tunable ion mobility through a radio-frequency confinement region. The resistive multipoles may include distributed-resistance electrodes or segmented resistive coatings that establish smooth DC gradients, enabling ion compression, expansion, attenuation, or temporal spreading while maintaining radial confinement. Such operation permits controlled reduction of instantaneous ion current without excessive ion loss or mass discrimination.

Further embodiments include wide bore confinement channels configured to accommodate large ion populations at reduced charge density. The wide bore channels may comprise RF multipoles, electrostatic confinement structures, gas-filled guides, or hybrid ion funnels having enlarged internal apertures. By increasing confinement volume, the channels reduce Coulombic interactions, improve transmission of high-abundance species, and preserve quantitative response over an expanded concentration range.

Additional embodiments employ long-life time-of-flight detectors configured for high cumulative ion dose operation. The detectors may include extended-area conversion surfaces, replaceable or regenerable emissive elements, gain-distributed microchannel plate assemblies, secondary-electron multipliers operated at reduced gain, or hybrid analog/counting readout circuits. Detector control may dynamically adjust gain, integration time, or ion packet intensity based on predicted or measured ion abundance.

In combined operation, the trap arrays, resistive multipoles, wide bore confinement channels, and long-life TOF detectors cooperate to expand usable dynamic range by distributing ions in space and time, minimizing space-charge effects, regulating ion packet intensity, and extending detector operating lifetime. The disclosed systems and methods are applicable to time-of-flight, orthogonal acceleration TOF, tandem mass spectrometry, ion mobility-mass spectrometry, and high-throughput analytical platforms requiring accurate measurement of trace and highly abundant analytes in the same acquisition.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise patent application abstract for a mass spectrometer with multiple operation modes: time separation of wide m/z ion flows, MR-TOF spectral segmentation, fragmentation for comprehensive MS-MS, and conventional operation.
counterfactuals.output: A mass spectrometer is provided having a plurality of selectable operating modes enabled by configurable ion optics, pulsed elements, fragmentation devices, and a controller. In a first mode, ions spanning a wide mass-to-charge range are temporally separated into ion-flow portions prior to analysis. In a second mode, a multi-reflection time-of-flight analyzer is operated to acquire segmented spectra corresponding to selected temporal or mass-to-charge windows. In a third mode, selected ions or ion-flow portions are fragmented to generate product ions for comprehensive MS-MS analysis across an extended mass-to-charge range. In a fourth mode, the instrument performs conventional mass analysis without temporal separation, spectral segmentation, or fragmentation. The controller coordinates ion transmission, trapping, pulsing, reflection timing, fragmentation, and detection to switch between modes or combine modes within an acquisition sequence, thereby improving dynamic range, resolving power, duty cycle, and analytical coverage for complex samples.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an invention disclosure paragraph about a tandem MR-TOF mass spectrometer designed for large charge throughput, reduced spectral population at the analyzer entrance, encoded orthogonal acceleration, and practical novel components.
counterfactuals.output: Disclosed is a tandem multi-reflection time-of-flight (MR-TOF) mass spectrometer configured to provide high charge throughput while reducing instantaneous spectral population at the entrance of a high-resolution analyzer. The instrument includes an upstream accumulation, cooling, and pre-separation stage that receives large ion currents and divides or conditions the ion population before transfer to a downstream MR-TOF analyzer, thereby limiting space-charge effects, peak overlap, and detector saturation without sacrificing total duty cycle. In one embodiment, ions are accumulated in a radio-frequency ion guide or trap, optionally mass-windowed or mobility-filtered, and then injected into a first MR-TOF or time-dispersion section that temporally spreads or selects ions prior to delivery to a second, higher-resolution MR-TOF analyzer. The analyzer entrance is supplied by an encoded orthogonal acceleration assembly that converts a continuous or quasi-continuous ion beam into a sequence of ion packets using a predetermined temporal code, such as a pseudo-random, Hadamard, chirped, or multiplexed pulse pattern, allowing multiple packets to coexist in the analyzer while remaining computationally separable upon detection. Practical novel components include a high-capacity ion accumulator with low-aberration extraction optics, a gated ion attenuator or spectral population reducer positioned before the analyzer, a coded orthogonal accelerator with independently driven push, pull, and compensation electrodes, dynamically switched ion mirrors for packet routing or tandem operation, and a decoding controller synchronized with detector acquisition to reconstruct mass spectra from overlapping encoded flight-time signals. The disclosed architecture enables substantially greater usable ion charge per measurement cycle than conventional MR-TOF systems while preserving resolving power, mass accuracy, and dynamic range, and is particularly useful for complex mixtures, trace analysis, proteomics, isotope analysis, and other applications requiring both high sensitivity and controlled spectral occupancy.
